newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates end higher, seen firm.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates end higher, seen firm.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates ended higher on Monday on tight market liquidity despite fund injection by the central bank, dealers said, adding they expected the rates to remain firm.
The overnight interbank rate closed at 8.319 percent against Saturday's 8.219 finish, with the 30-day commercial paper jumping to 8.00-8.50 against 8.25.

The central bank injected T$9 billion in funds into the banking system through open market operations to try to ease liquidity, but fear that there was not enough fund in the market had kept the rates high, dealers said.
Dealers said the rise was due mainly to increased demand of funds from stock investors eager to cash in on Taiwan's red hot bourse.
On Monday, the weighted index closed 2.18 percent or 168.67 points higher at 7,908.61, marking the market's highest close since it ended at 7,927.17 on May 17, 1990.
Dealers said cash demand will remain strong on Tuesday.
Trading interest was thin in the bond market due to investors' shift of focus to the local bourse.
The 10-year 86/4 bond yield was at 6.0950-1025 percent against 6.1000. -- James Lin (2-5080815)
